raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Building another SDPA plan for an already-loaded adapter and kernel repeats Python signature inspection. Cache the immutable parameter names and template host argument order by function identity, with bounded caches shared across plans. A replaced function gets its own entry, and each plan still receives its own mutable argument-order list.

Keep the compiled-wrapper ABI check per plan. The caches do not retain adapter instances or compiled launchables, and execution still validates and binds the current tensors, workspace and stream. Public APIs, eligibility, heuristics, native bindings and kernels are unchanged.

Validation on B200 with cuDNN 9.27 and public CuTeDSL 4.8.0:

- All 123 selected existing prepared-execution tests pass on both baseline and candidate, including O/LSE, pointer/workspace rebinding, shape overrides, FP8 scales and CUDA Graph capture/replay.
- Six new cases in two existing test files fail on the baseline and pass with this change. They cover reuse across plans, replacement entry points, all prepared host variants, independent slot lists and compiled-wrapper ABI rejection.
- The warmed graph-construction probe performs one signature inspection for the current compiled-wrapper check instead of six. Neither execute path performs signature inspection.
- Scoped formatting/license hooks pass. No timing threshold or heuristic-order golden was added.

No blocker found. This is a useful, bounded plan-construction optimization: immutable metadata is keyed by the function object, each plan receives a fresh argument-order list, and compiled-wrapper ABI validation still runs per plan. Runtime tensors, workspace and streams remain per-call inputs. The measured benefit is in constructing another plan for warmed kernels, not in steady-state execution. This is an author-account self-review; independent approval remains separate.

At the baseline [`ad0e1d7`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/ad0e1d7ea47e8d70d3813581d1300e7ab962e6b7/python/cudnn/sdpa/fwd/engines.py#L3117), `lower_dsl_prefill()` already imports `_torch_stream_context` from `api_dsl`. The changed line imports `_parameter_names` from that same module, in the same function scope. It does not move the import to module initialization. Resolving adapters remains a lowering-time operation; capability probing still keeps the DSL dependency lazy.

I compared the baseline/head import ASTs for all three changed production modules: there are no added cuDNN module dependencies or changed cuDNN import scopes. The new module-level dependencies are only the standard-library `inspect` and `functools`. The exact-head SM100 preparation/execution tests also passed, including the new entry-replacement/ABI checks.

I am leaving this existing lazy dependency unchanged; no source change or CodeQL suppression is needed for this line-only re-report. Independent approval and the running GPU CI remain separate requirements.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `2da8000c81c6` against base `ad0e1d7ea47e`.

No blocker found. This is a useful, bounded plan-construction optimization: immutable metadata is keyed by the function object, each plan receives a fresh argument-order list, and compiled-wrapper ABI validation still runs per plan. Runtime tensors, workspace and streams remain per-call inputs. The measured benefit is in constructing another plan for warmed kernels, not in steady-state execution. This is an author-account self-review; independent approval remains separate.

Validation: Exact-head SM100 run with verified source imports and public CuTe DSL 4.8.0: 31 selected tests passed, zero skips. Coverage includes all six new cache/entry-replacement/ABI cases plus existing dense/THD/FP8 preparation, shape overrides, fresh bindings, live scale values and CUDA Graph replay. Ran those six new tests against the unchanged baseline implementation with only the test files overlaid: all six fail for the intended repeated-inspection assertions, then pass on this head. No tolerance or expected ABI rejection was relaxed. Four fresh processes in head/base/base/head order, SM100 BF16 dense B=2/Hq=8/Hkv=2/Sq=128/Skv=256/D=128, PreparedDenseLaunch: warm full graph/plan construction medians were 3.206-3.217 ms on the baseline and 2.996-3.015 ms on this head, approximately 0.21 ms (6.4%) lower. Each process measured five batches of 20 constructions after warmup; graph release and GC were outside the timed interval. This excludes cold compilation. The same probe observed six signature inspections per warmed construction on the baseline versus one compiled-wrapper inspection on this head. Both execute paths perform zero signature inspections. A post-warmup cute.compile trap stayed silent across new plans, execution and replay. Separately measured CPU enqueue medians were 9.59-9.82 us and CUDA-event graph replay medians 11.91-12.24 us across the four processes; this bounded sample shows no material execution change. The existing FP32 reference checks passed, O/LSE hashes matched across all four processes, and 48 poisoned-buffer fixed-plan replays were bitwise repeatable. This is not a serving-throughput or cross-configuration determinism claim. Reviewed every new cache call site, immutable return values, function replacement semantics, independent mutable slot lists and the retained compiled-wrapper ABI check. Production kernels, native binding code, eligibility and heuristic ordering are unchanged. Precheck has no candidates and incremental diff check passes. Reused author-started CI 76466498; verified its exact head/trigger and all three changed production-file hashes.

Limitations: Current-head CI is still running. The independent native measurements cover SM100 and a bounded set of prepared paths, not every architecture or all cache-churn workloads. Construction timings reuse loaded modules and compiled artifacts. They do not establish an improvement to first-use compilation or steady-state inference latency.

Comment only: GitHub does not allow reviewing one's own PR with approval/request-changes.
